scope: Official Microsoft and Azure documentation supporting the Azure voice-agent storage, audio-format, compression, lifecycle, and performance research. Arithmetic derived from official format parameters is marked separately from Microsoft guidance.

material_claims.statement: Azure AI Speech real-time speech-to-text processes audio in server memory and does not store it at rest.
Voice Live API itself does not retain customer data by default, while connected services and features can have separate storage behavior.

Batch transcription reads input from customer-specified URLs. Results use a Microsoft-managed container by default, or a supported customer Azure container when destinationContainerUrl is provided; timeToLiveHours controls how long the transcription remains in the service after completion.
The preview Foundry voice-based prompt agent defaults store to false; store true persists transcript, event timeline, and raw audio together.
material_claims.qualification: Preview feature without an SLA; this switch is not documented as a raw Voice Live API session parameter.

material_claims.statement: The model is stateless, but optional Responses API, Threads, and Stored Completions features create a customer-resource data store for message history.
For prebuilt neural voices, input text and output audio are not stored in Microsoft logs.
material_claims.qualification: Custom voice, personal voice, and avatar paths have separate rules.

material_claims.statement: Foundry tracing is off by default and uses configured Application Insights and Log Analytics resources, while Voice Live support logging is a separate opt-in control with Microsoft-managed storage and a 30-day deletion period.

Azure Architecture Center stores recorded audio and processed call-center outputs in Blob Storage, optionally stores raw transcripts there, and tells Voice Live and GPT Realtime users to store conversation audio and transcripts in Blob Storage for analytics.
material_claims.qualification: The core architecture is post-call batch analytics. Voice Live and GPT Realtime storage appears in the article's alternatives section and is not default service persistence.

material_claims.statement: Blob access tiers include Hot, Cool, Cold, Archive, and Smart. Cool, Cold, and Archive have 30, 90, and 180 day minimum-duration guidance and early-deletion charges, while Smart automatically moves data among the Hot, Cool, and Cold online tiers.
Blob lifecycle policies can tier or delete matching blobs, but policy changes can take up to 24 hours to take effect and execution can be delayed near account limits.
Archive data is offline; for objects under 10 GB, standard rehydration can take up to 15 hours and high priority can complete in under one hour, subject to account-level throughput.

High-throughput block blob optimizations apply when Put Blob or Put Block uses a blob or block larger than 256 KiB; the target request rate is up to 3,000 requests per second for one block blob and up to 500 for one page blob.
material_claims.qualification: Targets are not guarantees and depend on concurrency, request size, tier, and source/destination speed.

material_claims.statement: Sequential blob naming can concentrate traffic on a hot partition; Azure recommends distributed naming, gradual ramp-up, and exponential-backoff retries.
Microsoft's Data Lake Storage guidance says analytics engines generally perform better with 256 MB to 100 GB files and describes aggregating small real-time files into larger analytics files.
material_claims.qualification: This is general analytics guidance, not a required size for individual voice recordings.

material_claims.statement: Speech SDK compressed input uses GStreamer to decode MP3, Ogg/Opus, FLAC, and telephony codecs locally before sending raw PCM to Speech.
Voice Live documentation describes 16 and 24 kHz input sampling with a 24 kHz default and SDK enums for PCM16 and G.711; Realtime 2.x documents headerless mono PCM16 at 24 kHz.
material_claims.qualification: The documented formats and sample rates vary by Voice Live page, deployed model, and API version.

material_claims.statement: Batch and fast transcription accept many compressed formats, but Microsoft recommends lossless WAV PCM or FLAC for best transcription quality.
Azure TTS guidance prioritizes streaming, connection reuse, first-byte metrics, and compressed transmission under constrained bandwidth.
Azure OpenAI Realtime documentation lists approximate latency of 100 ms for WebRTC, 200 ms for WebSocket, variable latency for SIP, and a 60-minute maximum session duration.
Azure Communication Services audio streaming documents 20 ms packets with 16-bit mono PCM at 16 or 24 kHz.
The Azure AI diagnostic logging overview does not establish a common guarantee that RequestResponse logs contain full prompts or audio bodies.
PCM and G.711 storage-size figures in the document are arithmetic derived from official sample rates, bit depths, and channel counts.
